## Answer

The volume and total surface area are

$$\boxed{V=\frac{18\pi}{35}},\qquad \boxed{S=\frac{16\pi}{5}}.$$

The inner curve is $y=(1-x^{2/3})^{3/2}$, so the washer formula gives

$$V=\pi\int_0^1\left[1-x^2-(1-x^{2/3})^3\right]dx=\frac{18\pi}{35}.$$

The outer quarter-circle generates a hemisphere of area $2\pi$. For the inner parametric arc, $ds=3\sin t\cos t\,dt$, hence

$$S_{\rm inner}=2\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^3t\,(3\sin t\cos t)dt=\frac{6\pi}{5}.$$

Adding both boundary surfaces gives $S=2\pi+6\pi/5=16\pi/5$.

## Answer

**B. It is a second-order infinitesimal relative to $x$.**

As $t\to0$,

$$t e^{\sin t}=t(1+t+O(t^2))=t+t^2+O(t^3).$$

Therefore

$$f(x)=\int_0^xte^{\sin t}dt=\frac{x^2}{2}+O(x^3),$$

so $f(x)\sim x^2/2$.

## Answer

$$\int_0^\infty\frac{x}{(1+x)^3}\,dx=\frac12.$$

This is the beta integral $B(2,1)=\Gamma(2)\Gamma(1)/\Gamma(3)=1/2$. It also follows directly by writing $x=(1+x)-1$ and integrating the two resulting powers.
